title: Quantum theory of laser noise in coherent-scattering levitated optomechanics
authors: Davide Candoli, Andreu Riera-Campeny, Lorenzo Dania, Oscar Schmitt Kremer, Johannes Piotrowski, Jayadev Vijayan, Lukas Novotny, Martin Frimmer, Oriol Romero-Isart, Carlos Gonzalez-Ballestero
abstract: State purity is a key resource for experimental tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects. Cavity cooling of a levitated nanoparticle via coherent scattering stands out as a strategy to prepare highly pure states of its roto-translational motion. In several cases, though, the performance of cooling by coherent scattering is limited by the classical fluctuations of the laser field. Here we present a quantum theory of coherent-scattering experiments which includes the effect of the laser amplitude and phase noise. We derive a master equation for the noise-averaged particle's dynamics, valid for both center-of-mass and rotational degrees of freedom, and quantify the cooling performance for different levels of noise in state-of-the-art experiments. We compute approximate analytical expressions for the laser-noise-induced heating rates and excess phonon number in both regimes of weak and strong optomechanical coupling. Moreover, our model can be applied to laser noise processes with generic power spectral densities and finite correlation times. This work offers a toolbox to quantify and optimize the state purity in coherent-scattering experiments, and opens new avenues towards the preparation of quantum states with levitated systems.
summary: This paper presents a quantum theory analyzing how laser noise limits the cooling and state purity of levitated nanoparticles in optomechanical cavities. By deriving a master equation incorporating laser amplitude and phase noise, the authors provide quantitative tools to optimize experimental performance. This advances the field by offering a comprehensive model for preparing quantum states with massive mechanical objects.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop a quantum theory to quantify and optimize the state purity of levitated nanoparticles cooled via coherent scattering, specifically addressing performance limitations imposed by classical laser field fluctuations.
main_result: The authors derive a master equation describing the particle dynamics under laser noise, providing a 'toolbox' to calculate laser-noise-induced heating rates and excess phonon numbers in both weak and strong optomechanical coupling regimes.
method: The analysis employs the Time-Convolutionless (TCL) master equation formalism, utilizing displacement transformations and applying weak-noise approximations to derive rate equations for the system's evolution.
model_or_system: The system is a dielectric nanoparticle undergoing roto-translational motion, cooled by coherent scattering within a Fabry-Pérot cavity. The model incorporates the particle-cavity Hamiltonian and treats laser amplitude and phase noise as stochastic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes.
key_observables: State purity, laser-noise-induced heating rates, excess phonon number, average cavity photon number, and particle displacement.
main_assumptions: The theory assumes laser noise processes have finite correlation times, and approximations are made in the weak-noise limit and the long-time limit ($t 	o \infty$) when using the TCL formalism.
figures_summary: Figure 1 sketches the physical setup: a dielectric nanoparticle trapped by an optical tweezer inside a Fabry-Pérot cavity, defining the system coordinates and phase encoding.
paper_structure: The paper builds the theory by first defining the system Hamiltonian and noise sources. It then analyzes the dynamics using the TCL formalism, deriving separate treatments for the weak-coupling and strong-coupling regimes, culminating in the final noise-averaged master equation.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and quantum optics as it provides a rigorous theoretical framework for quantifying decoherence sources (laser noise) in state-of-the-art quantum mechanical experiments involving macroscopic quantum systems.

The origin of coordinates coincides with the focus of the tweezer, which propagates in the z direction and is linearly polarized along x. The cavity axis forms an angle Θ with the y axis at the origin. The intensity of the cavity field at the particle’s position is encoded in the phase ϕ, with ϕ = 0 being an antinode and ϕ = π/2 a node.

Figure 2. Noisy mechanical driving induced by laser noise in a coherent scattering setup. We illustrate the two driving mechanisms in the particular case of the center-of-mass motion along z. Tweezer photons scattered off the particle transfer noise to the amplitude and phase of the cavity mode, encoded in the noisy displacement αcav(t). In turn, the fluctuations of the cavity field couple to the particle and drive its motion at a rate βc(t) (blue).
